newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND'S BACKS TO THE WALL VS NEW ZEALAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND'S BACKS TO THE WALL VS NEW ZEALAND.

text.p: England were fighting to save the match and their series lead on Monday at the end of the fourth day of their third and final cricket test against New Zealand.
Chasing 305 to win, England were 118 for two wickets at stumps with Mike Atherton, not out on 65, playing a classic captain's innings. With him was nightwatchman Andrew Caddick.
Only once -- against Australia in 1928/29 -- have England ever managed over 300 in the second innings to win.
With fine weather forecast for Tuesday, England need 187 to win with eight wickets standing. They lead the series 1-0 after winning the second test by an innings and 68 runs.

Atherton, who with 94 not out in the first innings became only the seventh England test batsman to carry his bat, received good support initially from Nick Knight and then Alec Stewart, but both fell to the left-arm spin of Daniel Vettori.
Just as England's hopes may hinge on Atherton, so New Zealand's are likely to rest on the shoulders of the 18 year-old left-arm spinner.
He extracted prodigious turn out of the rough at times and troubled all the batsmen, including Atherton. He finished with fine figures of two for 33 from his 23 overs.

In the morning session, New Zealand had resumed at a precarious 95 for six wickets and it was mainly thanks to Vettori, 29 not out, and Chris Cairns, with a typically swashbuckling 52, that the Kiwis reached 186 -- enough to provide a challenging total with their 118-run first innings lead. England began their chase with confidence, seeing off the new ball with few troubles.
Knight was severe on Heath Davis and New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming was forced to ring the changes to his attack.
However, Vettori bowling with fine control, received good support from part-timer Nathan Astle who was equally tight.
Knight on 29 was caught by Davis at mid-on when a Vettori ball dipped on him as he tried to loft it to the boundary.

Stewart, who made centuries in both the first two tests, grafted his way to 17. He was hit in the face by a rising delivery from Vettori and it was no surprise when he gave a bat-pad catch to Blair Pocock soon thereafter.
